Note: The exploded diagram of the cambox is provided for reference purposes only. The internal components of the cambox are not field-replaceable

Double arm: Moves tools to the carousel and the spindle.
Slide: Pushes against the tool to hold it in place during double arm movement.
Return spring: Pushes the slide against the tool.
Shim washers: Shims adjust the slide for proper clearance. If the slide is adjusted too tightly against the tool, it may not lock during rotation. If adjusted too

title: Side Mount Tool Changer (SMTC) - Double Arm / Cambox - Troubleshooting Guide - TG0128
text:
the tool.
Shim washers: Shims adjust the slide for proper clearance. If the slide is adjusted too tightly against the tool, it may not lock during rotation. If adjusted too loosely, tools will rock or fall out during rotation.
Adjuster rod: Locks the slide in place during a tool change.
Jam nut: This nut tightens against the slide to prevent the adjuster rod from rotating loose.
Plunger: Locks the adjuster rod during arm motion. The adjuster rod and slide cannot release the tool when the plunger is in the extended position.

Inspect the belt.

Alarm 628/673 ATC/TA ARM POSITIONING ERROR
Alarm 855 ATC ARM DRIVE-TRAIN FAILURE
-> The double arm's travel was obstructed. Check the double arm alignment. Move the obstructions or set a safe tool change position.
-> The spindle orientation is incorrect. Find the cause of the spindle orientation error.
-> The cambox is damaged. Test the cambox.
-> The values of Parameters 481 or 487 are incorrect in a machine with a servo-driven side-mount tool changer. Set the correct values (Parameter 481 = TT Grid Offset, Parameter 487 = TT Tool Change Offset).
-> The TRP quick exhaust is not functioning properly. Inspect and replace the quick exhaust if needed.

Tools fall out of the spindle side during a tool change.
-> The toolholders or pull studs are incorrect. Check for correct tool specifications.
-> The tool is too heavy. Check for correct tool weight specifications. Flag large or heavy tools.
-> The arm or plunger is worn. The double arm cannot correctly engage with the tool. Replace the worn parts in the double arm.
-> The spindle

-> The arm or plunger is worn. The double arm cannot correctly engage with the tool. Replace the worn parts in the double arm.
-> The spindle orientation is incorrect. Find the cause of the spindle orientation error.
-> The double arm is bent or damaged. Find the cause of the double arm bending. Straighten and smooth the double arm or replace it.
-> The gap between the tool holder and slide is not within specifications. Refer to: Side-Mount Tool Changer - Double Arm - Plunger and Adjuster Assembly - Inspection - Mill

Tools fall out of the arm during rotation.
-> The arm and plunger are worn. The double arm cannot correctly engage with the tool. Replace the worn parts in the double arm.

Tools fall out of carousel tool pockets.
-> The pocket spring or plungers are worn or damaged. Refer to: Side Mount (SMTC) - VF/VM/UMC/EC - Carousel and Pocket - Troubleshooting Guide

The cambox on a DT/DM is unable to rotate by hand.
-> The cambox will not be able to rotate by hand because it will eventually contact the rocker arm and try to unclamp the spindle. DO NOT replace the cambox because you are unable to rotate by hand; contact your local Haas Factory Outlet for further assistance.

EC/VC tool change cycle is very slow.
-> Parameter 223 Tool Changer Air Door Delay Change has a value; this should only have a value if a pneumatic door is present. Update configuration files to the latest, Parameter 223 will be set to zero. HSG-N 02-14-2023

Replacement double arm is not the correct length.
-> The incorrect double arm may have been ordered. Verify the correct part number and supersession has been ordered. Refer to the Double Arm Replacement Verification section.

Vertical Cambox's built June 15 2023 and later: Oil is leaking out of the cambox arm shaft. (Does not affect DT/DM/UMC-350 camboxes.)
-> There may be a problem with the exhaust check

text:
built June 15 2023 and later: Oil is leaking out of the cambox arm shaft. (Does not affect DT/DM/UMC-350 camboxes.)
-> There may be a problem with the exhaust check valve assembly. Starting in June 2023 a check valve is now included with the cambox exhaust assembly. Verify that the check valve is facing the correct way. HSG-N 07-12-2023

Corrosion inside of cambox.
-> The output shaft seal has gone bad and coolant has gotten into the cambox. Replace corroded parts inside of cambox. Replace the output shaft seal and check for scoring on the shaft. Refill the cambox with oil.

SMTC Double Arm Replacement Verification
Verify the double arm length: check that the replacement double arm is the correct length, measured center to center of the tool holder flange between the original and replacement double arm.
Verify that the double arm is the correct taper size and type: differentiate BT, CT, and HSK by V-flange shape.
Verify that the double arm has the correct key slot offset: casted double arm has the key slot machined at a 0 degree

title: Side Mount Tool Changer (SMTC) - Double Arm / Cambox - Troubleshooting Guide - TG0128
text:
BT, CT, and HSK by V-flange shape.
Verify that the double arm has the correct key slot offset: casted double arm has the key slot machined at a 0 degree angle position or at a 2.5 degree angled position; both use only a straight key instead of an offset key. HSG - 7/5/2023

Cambox Exhaust Check Valve
Verify the check valve arrow is facing away from the cambox. The check valve (PN 58-2754) should be installed between the brass fitting (PN 58-1674) and muffler fitting (PN 58-1865). HSG - 7/12/2023

Cambox Proximity Sensors
Corrective Action: Remove the carousel number plate to get access to the sensors. Go into manual tool recovery and push ATC FWD to move the arm through a complete cycle. Make sure the LED on the sensor and the diagnostic bit state change at the correct stage of the tool change cycle. If the sensors fail to change state, refer to the Proximity Sensor - Troubleshooting Guide.

Spindle Orientation
Corrective Action: Find the cause of the spindle orientation error. Make sure spindle drive and encoder belts have

title: Side Mount Tool Changer (SMTC) - Double Arm / Cambox - Troubleshooting Guide - TG0128
text:
change state, refer to the Proximity Sensor - Troubleshooting Guide.

Spindle Orientation
Corrective Action: Find the cause of the spindle orientation error. Make sure spindle drive and encoder belts have the correct tension. Make sure the spindle motor pulley and encoder pulley are not worn. Refer to VMC - Side-Mount Tool Changer - Spindle Orientation Offset - Parameter 257.

Double Arm Alignment
Corrective Action: Use a straightedge to find out if the arm is bent. Possible causes:
1. The tool release piston (TRP) sensor(s) are not adjusted correctly. If the TRP sensors are not adjusted correctly, a tool can get stuck in the spindle taper, or the drawbar might not release a tool. Damage to the double arm can occur. Adjust the tool release piston switches correctly.
2. The arm crashed into a rotary or a fixture during a tool change. Set a safe tool change position; move obstacles before the tool change.
3. A failed cambox position cable or sensor may cause the machine to think the arm is at the home position. The Z Axis comes down and

title: Side Mount Tool Changer (SMTC) - Double Arm / Cambox - Troubleshooting Guide - TG0128
text:
the tool change.
3. A failed cambox position cable or sensor may cause the machine to think the arm is at the home position. The Z Axis comes down and bends the arm.
Minor burrs or gouges on the double arm can visually be removed with a small file without needing replacement. If the double arm is not bent, check the double arm alignment. Refer to Side Mount (SMTC) - VMC - Double Arm - Alignment.

Cambox Drive Belt
Corrective Action: Inspect the belt for damage and replace it if necessary. Refer to VMC - Side-Mount Tool Changer (SMTC) - Carousel Motor - Replacement.

Toolholder and Pull Studs
Corrective Action: Refer to the correct pull stud and tool weight specifications. If you have a very heavy tool, install the Pocket slow down Service Kit (P/N 93-0254). This kit restricts the air exiting the pocket up/down cylinder to slow down the pocket.

Double Arm Plungers
Corrective Action: Inspect the plunger and adjuster assembly. Refer to Side-Mount Tool Changer - Double Arm - Plunger and Adjuster Assembly - Inspection. Refer to Video

title: Side Mount Tool Changer (SMTC) - Double Arm / Cambox - Troubleshooting Guide - TG0128
text:
pocket.

Double Arm Plungers
Corrective Action: Inspect the plunger and adjuster assembly. Refer to Side-Mount Tool Changer - Double Arm - Plunger and Adjuster Assembly - Inspection. Refer to Video - Side Mount Tool Changer (SMTC) Double Arm Maintenance for more information on how to maintain the double arm.

Cambox Test

Cambox Lost Motion Test: Go to Tool changer recovery. Rotate the double arm to clamp/unclamp position. Push and pull on the arm. Record the movement. Pull down and push up on the arm. Record the movement. There should be less than 1/4" (6 mm) of lost motion in the rotation or lift of the arm.

Cambox Internal Mechanical Test: Remove the cambox motor and rotate the pulley or coupling to cycle the cambox through a complete tool changer cycle. Listen for any abnormal internal noise when cycling the cambox. Run cambox forward or backwards looking for any particular section of binding. Check oil level while noting the viscosity and coloration of the oil. There should not be any binding in the cambox. You should be able to turn the

title: Side Mount Tool Changer (SMTC) - Double Arm / Cambox - Troubleshooting Guide - TG0128
text:
of binding. Check oil level while noting the viscosity and coloration of the oil. There should not be any binding in the cambox. You should be able to turn the pulley by hand. It will take more effort to turn the pulley when the output shaft is retracting. On a machine with a servo driven cambox it is necessary to re-set the double arm origin position after reinstalling the servo motor. Refer to the SMTC - Double Arm - Grid and Tool Change Offset procedure.

Double Arm Tool and Slide Adjustment
Push down on the plunger and hold it down. Put a tool holder into the arm. During correct operation, the slide moves in. Release the plunger. Try to remove the tool holder. During correct operation, the slide does not move in and the tool holder locks in position. Measure the space between the slide and the tool holder. Use a feeler gauge. The correct space is between 0.014 in (0.36 mm) and 0.020 in (0.51 mm). If the machine is a DM-1 or DT-1, the correct space is between

title: Side Mount Tool Changer (SMTC) - Double Arm / Cambox - Troubleshooting Guide - TG0128
text:
a feeler gauge. The correct space is between 0.014 in (0.36 mm) and 0.020 in (0.51 mm). If the machine is a DM-1 or DT-1, the correct space is between 0.005 in (0.13 mm) and 0.015 in (0.38 mm). Add or remove 0.01 in (0.25 mm) shim washers, part number 45-0075, until the space is correct. Once the gap is set reassemble the slider assembly with the spring and washer installed. Apply a layer of Lithium Tacky Grease to the finger, spring and washer.

MANUAL RECOVERY HOW TO: VMC - HMC - Side-Mount Tool Changer - Manual Recovery
1. Push [RESET] to clear any alarms. Push [RECOVER]. The control attempts an automatic recovery. Push [A].
2. If the automatic recovery attempt is not successful, the control gives you the (M) Manual recovery option. Push [M] for Manual.
3. The display shows suggestions to correct the problem. Follow the prompts as they are displayed. Use these commands to move the tool changer components: [ATC FWD]/[ATC REV] to turn the double arm; [UP]/[DOWN] cursor arrows to raise or lower the tool pocket;

title: Side Mount Tool Changer (SMTC) - Double Arm / Cambox - Troubleshooting Guide - TG0128
text:
they are displayed. Use these commands to move the tool changer components: [ATC FWD]/[ATC REV] to turn the double arm; [UP]/[DOWN] cursor arrows to raise or lower the tool pocket; [ORIENT SPINDLE] to reset and lock spindle orientation; [LEFT]/[RIGHT] cursor arrows to turn the carousel; [TOOL RELEASE] to trigger the tool clamp/unclamp.
4. If you push [ORIENT SPINDLE], the display shows a warning dialog box. Push [N] to cancel if the double arm will interfere with the spindle when it orients. Push [O] if it can safely be rotated and locked.
5. After the problem has been corrected, the display shows that no further actions are required. Push [C] to continue.
6. The Pocket Tool Table on the control displays the pocket currently in front of the spindle and the tool in the spindle. Make sure the tool in the spindle and current pocket match the control's display.
7. Push [MDI]. Push [ATC/FWD] to test the recovery. If the tool change recovery is not successful, it is most likely that the machine is mechanically jammed. Contact your Haas Factory Outlet

title: Side-Mount Tool Changer - Manual Recovery - Mill
text:
Side-Mount Tool Changer - Manual Recovery - Mill

Introduction
This procedure tells you how to perform a manual recovery on the Side-Mount Tool Changer (SMTC) of a Haas mill. A recovery is required if the SMTC cannot complete a tool change.

VMC - HMC - Side-Mount Tool Changer - Manual Recovery

1. Push [RESET] to clear any alarms. Push [RECOVER]. The control attempts an automatic recovery. Push [A].

2. If the automatic recovery attempt is not successful, the control gives you the (M) Manual recovery option. Push [M] for Manual.

3. The display shows suggestions to correct the problem. Follow the prompts as they are displayed. Use these commands to move the tool changer components: Push [ATC FWD] or [ATC REV] to turn the double arm. Push the [UP] or [DOWN] cursor arrows to raise or lower the tool pocket. Push [ORIENT SPINDLE] to reset the spindle orientation and lock it. Push the [LEFT] or [RIGHT] cursor arrows to turn the carousel left or right. Push the [TOOL RELEASE] button to trigger the tool clamp/unclamp.

4. If you push [ORIENT

title: Side-Mount Tool Changer - Manual Recovery - Mill
text:
it. Push the [LEFT] or [RIGHT] cursor arrows to turn the carousel left or right. Push the [TOOL RELEASE] button to trigger the tool clamp/unclamp.

4. If you push [ORIENT SPINDLE], the display shows a warning dialog box. Push [N] to cancel the spindle orientation if the tool changer double arm will interfere with the spindle when the spindle orients. If the spindle can safely be rotated and locked, push [O].

5. After the problem has been corrected, the display shows that no further actions are required. Push [C] to continue.

6. The Pocket Tool Table on the control displays the pocket that is currently in front of the spindle and the tool that is in the spindle. Make sure that the tool in the spindle and the current pocket match the control's display.

7. Push [MDI]. Push [ATC/FWD] to test the recovery. If the tool change recovery is not successful, it is most likely that the machine is mechanically jammed. Contact your Haas Factory Outlet for assistance.

title: Alarm 9973 Unstable Incoming Power
text: the 9973 alarm tells you that there is a problem with the incoming power supplied to the machine the Wye-Delta contactor here has one set of contacts closed and the other open at all times power from the i/o board here keeps the relevant contactor closed and conducting current if you experience a brownout in your shop the power keeping the contactor closed might sag momentarily allowing the contactor to open up if this happens while the circuit is under full load the contactor will arc and can cause serious damage to protect from this all Wye-Delta contactor assemblies built after August 2017 use a pair of auxiliary contacts here to monitor the open and close state of the main contacts this cable here connects these auxiliary contacts to the i/o PCB allowing the machine to check the status of the Y Delta contactor continuously if your machine generates a 9973 alarm it means the i/o board saw one of these contacts open when it should have been closed you will see the alarm on-screen and the Machine will stop
